title: A systematic zero error
caption: Extension against load should pass through the origin. This line crosses the extension axis at 3 mm: a constant offset, a zero error, perhaps from measuring length from the wrong point. The gradient, 4 mm N⁻¹, is unaffected.
alt: Five points of extension against load with error bars, the best-fit line meeting the extension axis at about 3 millimetres instead of zero.
description: Load 1 to 5 N; extensions 7.1, 10.9, 15.2, 18.8, 23.1 mm, each ± 0.3 mm.
Least-squares line: gradient 3.99 mm N⁻¹, intercept 3.05 mm.
Hooke's law predicts zero extension at zero load, so the intercept is a systematic error; it shifts every reading by the same amount and leaves the gradient unchanged.
